summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with worsening dyspnea and hypoxia two days after completing a course of moxifloxacin and a prednisone taper for a recent pneumonia. Despite treatment, his shortness of breath, cough, and sputum production had worsened. Imaging showed no new pneumonia but findings consistent with COPD exacerbation and possible Velcade-induced pneumonitis. He responded well to a high-dose steroid taper and a short course of antibiotics. A CT without contrast showed improvement in prior lung changes. An abdominal ultrasound revealed interval enlargement of his abdominal aortic aneurysm to 5.2 cm, prompting a vascular surgery follow-up. Warfarin was restarted, and Bactrim was resumed for Pneumocystis prophylaxis due to immunosuppression. He improved clinically, was weaned off supplemental oxygen, and discharged home with a steroid taper, antibiotics, and close follow-up.
problems: Abdominal aneurysm without mention of rupture
